channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakh President Emphasizes Teacher's Role in Shaping Responsible Citizens
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev highlighted the importance of raising a hardworking, knowledge-seeking, and inquisitive generation for the nation's future. He stressed the crucial role of teachers in forming educated, law-abiding, and honest citizens. The President also noted the growing national values of cleanliness, diligence, honesty, and mutual respect, as exemplified by the 'Clean Kazakhstan' campaign.

item.title: Kazakh President: Traditional Cinema Era Fading with AI and Digital Technologies
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev believes the era of traditional filmmaking is declining due to AI and digital advancements. He stressed that reading remains vital for societal development and serves as a 'spiritual shield' for youth. Tokayev noted the global significance of the Astana AI Film Festival, highlighting AI's potential in cinema creation.

item.title: Kazakh President Congratulates Teachers, Discusses Education and Future Generations
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev congratulated Kazakh teachers on their professional holiday, emphasizing their pivotal role. He highlighted the construction of over 1,300 new schools and the importance of qualified educators. Tokayev also stressed the significance of reading as a 'spiritual shield' and announced a forthcoming national concept for developing reading culture.

item.title: President Tokayev Emphasizes Book Reading as a Spiritual Shield for Youth
item.description: Speaking at a ceremony for Teachers' Day, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev highlighted the importance of reading for young people. He noted recent events in Astana on artificial intelligence, including the AI & Digital Bridge forum and the Astana AI Film festival, showcasing AI's role in filmmaking.

item.title: President Tokayev Urges Teachers to Instill Value of Knowledge and Hard Work in Students
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with educators, emphasizing that life is not a fairy tale and deep knowledge is crucial for success. He stressed the importance of teachers guiding children towards becoming open, educated, and responsible citizens, and providing real opportunities for their future.

item.title: Moscow Format Consultations on Afghanistan Convene Regional Powers in Russia
item.description: The eighth Moscow Format meeting on Afghanistan began in Moscow, gathering regional countries to discuss security and economic cooperation. Representatives from Afghanistan, China, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Russia, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan are attending. Russia's Foreign Minister Lavrov praised the Taliban's governance.

item.title: Kazakhstan Strengthens Human Rights Protection Principles into Concrete Actions
item.description: Kazakhstan is consistently strengthening legal guarantees for human rights protection and developing humanitarian cooperation. An expert notes that fulfilling international obligations, diplomatic initiatives, and providing practical assistance to people in crisis situations define Kazakhstan's responsible stance on the international stage.

item.title: Hazaras in Afghanistan Face Loss of Life and Land, Genocide Watch Reports
item.description: Genocide Watch reports that the Hazara people in Afghanistan are facing the loss of their lives and their land. The specific details of the situation and the nature of the threats are not elaborated in the provided text.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Tokayev Summarizes Education Reform: AI Lessons and Increased Scholarships
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev reviewed Kazakhstan's education reform, highlighting the construction of 1,342 new schools and the introduction of AI lessons. Student scholarships have increased 2.5 times, and over 15,000 teachers, half of them young specialists, were employed.

item.title: Latvia May Temporarily Suspend Visa Issuance to Uzbek Citizens
item.description: Latvia may temporarily suspend issuing visas to citizens of Uzbekistan. This decision is reportedly due to several crimes, including those against minors, committed by Uzbek nationals shortly after arriving in the country. Further details are expected regarding the potential suspension and its implications.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Receive Compensation in Long-Standing Dunga Field Dispute Settlement
item.description: An agreement has been signed in Astana to resolve disputes concerning the Dunga field production sharing agreement. Kazakhstan will receive financial compensation, and conditions will be created for continued investment in the asset's development. This settlement allows for the practical implementation of a new field development plan for 2026-2039, projecting the extraction of 67.4 million barrels of oil.

item.title: Azerbaijan, Turkey, and Uzbekistan Conduct Large-Scale Joint Military Exercises 'Unity Force-2026'
item.description: Thousands of military personnel from Azerbaijan, Turkey, and Uzbekistan, along with observers, participated in the 'Unity Force-2026' exercises in Azerbaijan's Karabakh region. The drills simulated large-scale drone attacks, cyberattacks, disinformation, and vessel hijacking scenarios. Over 3,500 troops were involved, utilizing advanced military equipment and focusing on modern warfare tactics, including drone operations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Monitors Situation in Russia's Irkutsk Region Amidst Suspected Plague Case
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health is monitoring the situation in Russia's Irkutsk region following the death of an employee from the Anti-Plague Institute. Preventive measures and sanitary-quarantine checks are intensified at border crossings. The ministry assesses the risk of infection entering Kazakhstan as low, with enhanced controls also reported in Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Lawyer Reports Possible Pressure and Deteriorating Conditions for Detained Activist Sanzhar Bokeyev
item.description: The lawyer for Kazakh activist Sanzhar Bokeyev, detained since March 18, has reported a sharp decline in his living conditions and possible physical and psychological pressure. His lawyer stated that Bokeyev and other defendants were moved to Astana and placed in harsh conditions, including being shaved and held in cold cells. The lawyer suspects Bokeyev may have been beaten.

item.title: Tajikistan Achieves Significant Medal Count Increase at Asian Games in Japan
item.description: Tajikistan secured 16 medals at the XX Summer Asian Games in Japan, more than doubling its previous total of seven. While the number of gold medals remained the same, the overall performance marked a significant step forward for the nation. Among Central Asian countries, Tajikistan showed the greatest progress compared to the previous games.

item.title: Empty Bike Lanes Amid Traffic Jams Spark Debate in Almaty
item.description: Empty bicycle lanes alongside severe traffic congestion have reignited public debate in Almaty regarding the city's road space allocation. A blogger's video highlighted this disparity, showing cars stuck in traffic while adjacent bike lanes remained largely unused. This situation raises questions about the efficiency of micro-mobility infrastructure.

item.title: Taliban Begins Arms and Drone Purchases from Belarus; India Reportedly Mediates
item.description: The Taliban has reportedly begun purchasing weapons and drones from Belarus, according to media reports. Afghan former officials suggest this follows a pattern from the Ashraf Ghani era. India, which has a contentious relationship with Pakistan, is reportedly mediating these deals, raising geopolitical questions.

item.title: Ministry Responds to Video of Military Mess Hall Lacking Meat and Bananas
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Defense has addressed a viral video showing soldiers' meals lacking meat and bananas, sparking online criticism. The ministry explained the video was filmed during a training exercise where meals were delayed and cooled. They confirmed the food was reheated and served properly after the issue was identified.

item.title: Heavy rain causes road collapse in Almaty, disrupting traffic and sparking public anger
item.description: A section of road in Almaty collapsed after heavy rainfall and repair work, causing significant traffic jams. Residents expressed dissatisfaction with the quality of road repairs, with some vehicles getting stuck in the resulting pothole.

item.title: Almaty LRT construction site asphalt collapses after heavy rain, causing traffic jams
item.description: Following heavy rainfall, asphalt at an LRT construction site in Almaty subsided and collapsed, trapping several vehicles and causing traffic congestion. The road infrastructure department stated that restoration work is underway using temporary measures.

item.title: At least five killed in Ahal road accident involving bus and truck
item.description: A collision between a bus and a truck in Turkmenistan's Ahal province resulted in at least five fatalities, according to RFE/RL's correspondent. Turkmen.news reported eight deaths, including four teenagers returning from football training.

item.title: Astana Considers Raising Public Transport Fares to 150 Tenge
item.description: Astana's city administration is proposing to increase public transport fares from 110 to 150 tenge for cashless payments starting December 1st. The administration cited rising operational costs for carriers, including fuel, spare parts, and driver wages, as the reason for the proposed hike.

item.title: Kazakhstan's tenge weakens against dollar due to external factors
item.description: The Association of Financiers attributes the tenge's sharp decline to falling oil prices and a strengthening dollar globally. Increased demand for dollars from Kazakh citizens may also have contributed. The dollar reached 451.50 tenge, a significant rise after weeks of tenge appreciation.

item.title: Tajikistan modernizes seismic stations with new digital equipment
item.description: Tajikistan is upgrading its seismic stations with new digital equipment as part of a modernization program. New equipment has been installed at the Boghidzhugda and Sarband stations. This initiative, supported by the World Bank, aims to enhance seismic data analysis and risk assessment capabilities.

item.title: Head of Court in Kazakhstan's Kyzylorda Region Sentenced to 9 Years for Corruption
item.description: The head of a court and a judge in Kazakhstan's Kyzylorda region have been sentenced to nine years in prison for corruption offenses, the National Security Committee (KNB) reported. They were found guilty of accepting a large bribe, with the judge allegedly receiving 6 million tenge to grant a suspended sentence to a fraudster, and an additional 300,000 tenge for full release.

item.title: Iran Envoy: Afghanistan and Iran Share Common Opportunities and Threats
item.description: Iran's deputy ambassador in Kabul, Seyed Hassan Mortazavi, stated that Iran and Afghanistan face shared opportunities and threats due to current regional and global developments. He emphasized the need for close cooperation to address common challenges and safeguard mutual interests, including security, economic matters, and border cooperation.

item.title: Former Kazaly District Court Chairman and Judge Sentenced for Bribery
item.description: The former chairman and a judge of the Kazaly District Court in the Kyzylorda region have been sentenced to nine years in prison each. The National Security Committee reported they were found guilty of corruption offenses, including accepting large bribes. They were apprehended in January.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Oil Industry Successfully Postpones Fuel Excise Tax Increase
item.description: Kazakhstan's oil industry, through the PetroMining Association, has convinced the government to postpone the planned increase in excise taxes on petroleum products. The increase, which would have raised rates from 50% to 95% of the price difference, is now delayed from January 1, 2027.

item.title: Daurenbek Yryskali Appointed President of "Otanadastar" Fund
item.description: Daurenbek Yryskali has been appointed president of the "Otanadastar" Fund, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan. Born in 1963, Yryskali has held various diplomatic positions since 1993, including consul general in Omsk and counselor-envoy in Germany.

item.title: Iranian Oil Minister Mohsen Khojastehmehr Resigns; Hamid Bovard Appointed Acting Minister
item.description: Iranian Oil Minister Mohsen Khojastehmehr resigned on October 4 for personal reasons, which President Masoud Pezeshkian eventually accepted. Hamid Bovard, formerly deputy oil minister, has been appointed acting oil minister. Khojastehmehr had served since August 2024.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rakhmon Calls for Increased Use of Tajik Language Online
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rakhmon has urged for the expanded use of the Tajik language, particularly on the internet, in a message for State Language Day. He emphasized the language's role in national identity, culture, and unity, noting its development over 35 years of independence. The president highlighted government initiatives, including laws and programs, aimed at strengthening the language's status.

item.title: Economist: Traffic Congestion in Uzbekistan is a State Policy Issue Requiring Solutions
item.description: Economist Islombek Niyozmetov stated that traffic congestion in Uzbekistan's cities, particularly Tashkent, has become a significant problem. He emphasized that traffic is not merely an inconvenience but a critical issue that requires attention at the state policy level, necessitating comprehensive solutions to address its socio-economic impacts.

item.title: UNESCO Calls for Increased Support for Teachers on World Teachers' Day
item.description: On World Teachers' Day, UNESCO urged greater support and improved professional status for teachers globally. The organization highlighted challenges like digital technologies, climate change, and migration, emphasizing the need for better working conditions and recognition for effective role performance.

item.title: Tajikistan Plans 800 MW "Khutalon" Hydroelectric Power Station Construction
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Energy and Water Resources visited the planned site for the "Khutalon" (Shurob) hydroelectric power station. The facility, with a projected capacity of 800 MW and an annual output exceeding 2.5 billion kWh, will be built on the Vakhsh River between the Rogun and Nurek HPPs. The project aims to increase the country's energy generation capacity and optimize hydropower resource utilization.

item.title: Russian Tank Crews Practice Engaging Simulated Enemy in Tajikistan Drills
item.description: Russian tank crews of the T-72B3M variant successfully engaged simulated targets during the 'Center-2026' strategic command and staff exercises in Tajikistan. The drills took place on the 'Lyaur' mountain training ground, utilizing terrain for cover and employing tactics like 'fire carousel'.

item.title: UN Official Discusses Governance, Regional Peace, and Migrant Return with Afghan Deputy Minister
item.description: Rosemary DiCarlo, UN Under-Secretary-General for Political and Peacebuilding Affairs, met with Afghanistan’s Deputy Minister of Urban Development and Housing in Kabul. Discussions covered governance, regional stability, housing, Afghan migrant return, and Afghanistan-Pakistan transit routes. DiCarlo affirmed the UN's continued support for the Afghan people.

item.title: Tax Inspectors in Qashqadaryo Accused of Embezzling Over 122 Million Soums
item.description: Tax inspection employees in Qarshi city, Qashqadaryo region, have been exposed for embezzling funds from taxpayers. According to the Department for Combating Economic Crimes under the General Prosecutor's Office, nine tax inspectors allegedly accepted 122.6 million soums from 97 taxpayers, failing to credit the funds to their accounts and instead misappropriating them. A criminal case has been initiated.

item.title: Human Rights Watch: US Should Provide Reparations to Victims of 20-Year War in Afghanistan
item.description: Human Rights Watch is calling on the United States to provide reparations and accountability for victims of the 20-year war in Afghanistan. The organization stated that the US has a responsibility to address the harm caused by its military actions and policies during the conflict. This call comes amid ongoing discussions about the future of Afghanistan and the international community's role.

item.title: Kazakh President reshuffles military leadership after 14 soldiers' deaths
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev continues to reshuffle the military leadership following the deaths of 14 servicemen. New appointments include Aytkurman Omarbekov as Chief of the General Staff and First Deputy Minister of Defense, and Azamat Khasenov as Deputy Head of the State Security Service. Several other high-ranking officers were dismissed.

item.title: ADB Allocates $20.5 Million for Tajikistan's Pension Sector Amid Middle East Tensions
item.description: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved $20.5 million in financial assistance for Tajikistan's pension and social services sector. This funding, part of ADB's support for countries affected by Middle East economic and financial tensions, aims to improve pension services, modernize payment systems, and enhance social assistance accessibility.
